answer: An agent may wander between opal auctions and ember alerts, but its voting weight must follow locked tokens. Validators check a ledger lock naming one key and epoch, reject reuse of its output, and count one vote per lock. Splitting 1,000 tokens among ten keys still buys only 1,000 units of weight; every additional identity also needs its own minimum bond. Conflicting signed votes for one lock prove fraud and burn that bond. Parallel keys cannot multiply the same collateral. This assumes a scarce token, correct lock accounting and stake-proportional influence.
